mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates for future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 7.0% over a one-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of central bank rate cuts and reduces recession risk premiums, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative or flat 5-day returns in 60% or more of instances where UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in private demand, which triggers a policy response from the Fed and reduces long-term real interest rates, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS fall below thresholds (t-test p > 0.05), or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which increases the probability of a Fed rate cut and reduces the risk of inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat in 60% or more of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over a one-month window signals a tightening cycle, which increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during high-FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real personal consumption (RSAFS) and residential construction (HOUST) above their 12-month highs signals strong private demand, which increases inflationary pressure and raises the likelihood of a Fed rate hike, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST exceed thresholds (t-test p > 0.05), or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 135,000 in a single month signals a labor market slowdown, which increases the probability of a Fed rate cut and reduces long-term real rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during PAYEMS declines (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past five months, with a year-over-year decline, signals a deepening economic slowdown, which increases the likelihood of aggressive fiscal and monetary stimulus, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during GDPC1 contractions (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
